prompt.context: After the September 11, 2001 incident, air travel in the US declined to unforeseen levels and most of the airlines were looking at all possible ways to cut costs. Our client is an airline which had cut the free meal provided to passengers. It is year 2003 and now the client wants to introduce retail sales of meals, beverages and snacks on the plane for which the passengers will pay. The client has not thought through any of the options, risks and opportunities and have called you at the very thought of this introduction.
prompt.question: To introduce this retail food and beverage program, what are your considerations from an operational perspective?

clarifying_info.q: Should we evaluate whether this initiative is worth pursuing at all?
clarifying_info.a: The decision to 'Go' has already been made. Focus only on operational considerations for implementation.

framework: Material flow — what items to sell, where to source them, inventory levels, freshness, distribution to the plane
Cash flow — payment methods (cash, credit/debit), connectivity infrastructure, collection and reconciliation with accounting
Information flow — integration of passenger data with procurement, accounting system updates, warehouse/distribution inventory monitoring
People and capabilities — staffing levels, training on inventory and cash handling, order-taking process, ownership of inventory and cash management

questions.prompt: Walk through the material flow considerations for this program.
questions.guidance: Candidate should identify: what items to sell (meals, beverages, packaged foods, snacks); make-vs-buy decision (in-house kitchen vs. buying from major retailers, especially if focusing on snacks); how much inventory to stock per flight; the distribution system from supplier to aircraft; how to maintain food freshness and a spoilage/disposal policy; and how to tailor item selection by flight type (long-haul vs. short-haul vs. point-to-point).

questions.prompt: Walk through the cash flow considerations.
questions.guidance: Candidate should address: whether passengers pay in cash, credit card, or debit card; if credit/debit, what connectivity (hardware, network) is needed on board and how to ensure reliability; how collected funds are remitted to and reconciled with the corporate accounting department.

questions.prompt: Walk through the information flow considerations.
questions.guidance: Candidate should cover: integrating passenger manifest/booking data with the procurement function so inventory matches expected demand; determining frequency and method for pushing sales data into accounting systems; monitoring inventory levels at distribution centers and warehouses.

questions.prompt: Walk through the people and capabilities considerations.
questions.guidance: Candidate should address: whether current cabin crew headcount is sufficient; training requirements for handling inventory, cash, and card transactions; the process for taking orders (pre-take-off vs. on-demand, number of cabin passes); and assigning clear ownership/accountability for inventory and cash on each flight.

questions.prompt: Summarize your key points in 30 seconds.
questions.guidance: Candidate should concisely recap the four operational pillars — material flow, cash flow, information flow, people — and highlight one or two critical risks (e.g., spoilage, connectivity reliability, staff training) before closing with a crisp recommendation or next step.

recommendation: Proceed with the retail food and beverage program by addressing all four operational pillars in parallel: secure a reliable supply and distribution chain, implement a payment collection system with robust connectivity, integrate procurement with passenger data systems, and train cabin crew before launch.
risks: Food spoilage and waste if inventory planning is inaccurate
Unreliable in-flight payment connectivity causing transaction failures
Insufficient cabin crew capacity to manage sales alongside safety duties
Data integration gaps leading to procurement mismatches with actual demand
next_steps: Define the product assortment and make-vs-buy sourcing decision
Pilot payment hardware and connectivity on a small number of routes
Develop staff training modules for inventory handling and payment processing
Design integration between booking/passenger systems and procurement/inventory systems
